div.h1: Transitive closure, and how to charge for it
div.p: What every dl6 program is an instance of, what the shootout measures, and the recurrence a defect swapped in behind our backs.

g.text: 3 · Two ways to charge for the same answer
7 · Why the checksum is a set function
9 · The rail that closes the gap

div.p: a finite directed graph
the reachability relation: every pair joined by a path of length one or more
Every recursive dl6 rule is this shape with a different join. Fix the cost here and every recursive head inherits it.
clause one seeds the relation with the edges themselves
clause two composes what is known with one more edge
The chain is monotone and bounded above by a finite set, so it stops. It stops at the first repeat, and that repeat is the answer.
k is what a per-round evaluator pays for, and the families were chosen to spread it by three orders of magnitude.
Round n composes everything known so far with E.
Round n composes only what round n-1 newly produced.
The two differ by a factor of k, the recursion depth. On grid_10000, k = 88.
__frontier_reachable holds the delta.
Nothing retired the frontier between rounds, and the filter _phase >= 0 admits every row ever staged.
The last column tracks the third, never the second. Pass 43 has an empty delta and still charges 87 ms.

div.h3: The compiler had written it months ago
div.p: supportSql carried the closure as one recursive query. retractionGuardSql only let it run when a delta carried a retraction, so a purely additive tick fell through to the round loop.

g.text: SELECT b0."source", b1."target" -- dedup IS the delta
WHERE b1."source" = b0."target") -- step: Rn o E

div.h3: Why UNION buys semi-naive for free
div.p: SQLite keeps the queue of rows it has yet to expand and drops duplicates on insert. A pair enters the queue exactly once, which is the same accounting as the delta.
grid_10000, 1,069,200 rows, 9d7239568960d6a8 on all three.
harness/src/gen.rs, seeded and deterministic. Three families, parameters TUNED per scale so every case lands in the band.

div.h3: The three families isolate different k
Every entrant speaks one wire contract
div.p: Three JSONL lines on stdout, nothing else, ever.

div.h3: The lemma that makes paging sound
div.p: Comparing engines needs one number per ANSWER, and the answer is a set. Any digest that depends on enumeration order compares implementations rather than results.

div.h3: Corollary, used to fix a real OOM
div.p: Any partition of R folds to the same number, so the driver can read the head table in pages and drop each one.

div.h3: An answer is trusted when three different things agree

div.p: harness/src/refengine.rs, deliberately naive. Anchors truth at the 10k cases and is never timed.
Grades: derived and checksum.
v6/prolog/conformance/, the language definition itself. 420 fixtures, tick log compared byte for byte.
mono, rxgraph, interp. Any disagreement on (derived, checksum) fails the whole run and no standings are written.
chain_10000 -> df09b2f409f8b9a8 on dl6 AND mono.
Every oracle above grades the answer. A naive closure returns the right answer, so it passes all three while paying a factor of k.

div.h3: Grade the RECURRENCE, not the answer
div.p: A one-pass closure issues a statement count independent of k. A per-round loop issues one insert plus its staging per round.
Chain of n edges fed as ONE arrival batch, closure is n(n+1)/2 rows.
Slope 4 against slope 0. Non-vacuity: 6 / 36 / 136 rows derived. A COUNT, never a timing, so it cannot flake.

div.h3: So the ladder prices the CONSTANT, not the algorithm
div.p: chain_10000, 9,996,213 rows, df09b2f409f8b9a8 on every row.

tr.td: a u32 pair in a hash set

div.p: dl6 is 203x behind mono, down from 6,832x this morning.
Zero of the 38.4x came from a better algorithm. All of it came from deleting work that bought nothing: a factor of k the frontier was charging, and rows that crossed into V8 only to be discarded.
What remains is the price of durability and generality, which is a thing to buy on purpose.
